hints.title: Top Seller Revenue Identification
hints.text: Calculate total revenue generated by each seller across all transactions, identifying the highest aggregate earners.

hints.title: Having Filter on Maximum Aggregate
hints.text: Group sales by seller identifier and retain sellers whose summed price matches the global maximum seller total.

hints.title: Sales Analysis Query Blueprint
hints.text: select seller_id from Sales group by seller_id having sum(price) = (select sum(price) from Sales group by seller_id order by sum(price) desc limit 1).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT seller_id
FROM Sales
GROUP BY seller_id
HAVING SUM(price) = (
    SELECT SUM(price)
    FROM Sales
    GROUP BY seller_id
    ORDER BY SUM(price) DESC
    LIMIT 1
);
```

complexity.notes: Grouped aggregation and scalar subquery limit operation run in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple LIMIT 1 ignores revenue ties where multiple sellers share top earnings.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Subquery aggregation evaluates maximum revenue once, avoiding Cartesian joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of HAVING clause with subquery or DENSE_RANK() window function to handle ties.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def sales_analysis(sales: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    totals = sales.groupby('seller_id')['price'].sum().reset_index()
    max_val = totals['price'].max()
    return totals[totals['price'] == max_val][['seller_id']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Groupby Sum and Max Filtering
